Title: Minicon Last Staurday, or The Rise of the Ravnos

Messages.Author: hamdamcwa
Messages.Body:
I had a close call on Saturday. I told myself that, since I've had
such an AWFUL run lately, if I failed to score any VPs at Minicon
(London, UK) last Saturday, I would sell my cards and live somewhere
as far away from VTES as possible, in a sulk. I scored 3 on the day,
and just squeezed into the final (where I lasted all of 2 minutes -
more later), so I feel a bit more confidant. All my Dan Murdocks,
!Tremere Vampires, and Complete Collection (MUST SEE - HUGE COLLECTION
(tm)) is safe. For now...

It was a fine September day when 12 brave souls walked onto the field
of combat. A good standard of player, and a newbie too!

Mike Nudd, as well as organising, was playing the Sleaziest Setite
Deck... EVER! Much use of Nephertiti, Crowbar Towers, Temptations, and
Stealth Bleed. Yuerck!

Jackie Eves was playing a Potence Gangrel Rush deck. Mid range vamps
and lots of Potence, topped off with a smattering of Claws. Nice.

Adam Payne Chickened out of playing his much promised Jimmy Dunn deck
(*JimmyDunn, JimmyDunn, JimmyDunn-Dunn-Dunn*) and settled for a Ravnos
deck using the awesome power of the Starshell Grenade Launcher. Reduce
Stealth, Block, Range (Amia) and pop! A great deck, but suffered due
to the competition.

Legbiter was playing a Temptation of Greater Combat deck (votes, ToGP,
and a bit more combat than in previous incarnations). New boy Calebros
the Matyr and Sheldon featured heavily.

"New Boy" Tony was playing Assamites. Pretty much what you'd expect,
except lots of Fortitude.

Phil Mattingly was also playing a Ravnos weenie deck. This one had
lots of Attonements and Sniper Rifles.

Martin Cubberley was playing a Ventrue Potence rush / vote deck with a
nasty Hostile Takeover angle. Also Yeurgh!

Matt Green was playing a !Toreador deck with a splash of Obfuscate.
This has made a few appearances of late in friendly play and is
tighter than a ducks bum (this means it is a Good deck)! It uses a lot
of Suddens and Revelations to rob Preys of Pool gain, and then stealth
bleed them with Legal Manipulations.

Will Lee should be shot on sight for playing a HIDEOUS Theo Bell /
Beast rush deck with LOTS of Fortitude. Rush, Signpost, Grapple, slap,
Disarm, Decaptate. Yuck.

James Lewis was (bravely) playing weenie presence bleed / vote. It
died a death!

Simon Croome played a Protean/Dominate bleed deck using lots of
Gangrel / Gangrel Anti.

I played my Best Ever Gangrel deck. Lots of Big vampires with potence
and protean. Minion Tap / 5th to buy up Angus, Wynn and Ingrid. ToGP
vampires using Angus, rush vampires with Wynn in an Uncontrollable
Rage, Parity Shift with Ingrid. It sort-of worked 2 times, and got
nuked before I could even start by a Hostile for Martin Cubberley in
the second game.

Going into the Final, we had:

Legbiter on 6 points
Phil Mattingly on 5.5 points
Will Lee on 4 points
Matt Green on 5 points
David Hammond on 3 points (tied TPs, so on the toss of a coin)

In the final, I got smashed out by Will Lee (even AFTER being moved
around the table) giving Legbiter 1 point. Phil Mattingly, Will Lee,
and finally Legbiter got smashed by Matts Stealthy (!) bleeds, giving
Matt 4 points, and the day!

Well, here's some thoughts...

1) Lots of Independant action. Note that 4 players elected to go the
way of the independants, 2 of which were Ravnos. One Ravnos deck
actually made the final - the first to do so in the UK for as long as
I can remember. Huzzah!

2) We were, however, playing mainly 4 player games (except the final).
This made a huge difference to the environment.

3) As predicted in the Gangrel Newsletter, the Starshell Grenade
Launcher has started to make a wholesale appearance. They are Awesome!

4) Matt Greens first Tourney win in some time! Well done Matt...

5) Theo Bell with Fortitude. How broken is THAT!!! ;)

See y'all in the funny pages...

DH

Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson
Messages.Body:
On 1 Oct 2001 05:49:47 -0700, Dave Hammond wrote:

>2) We were, however, playing mainly 4 player games (except the final).
>This made a huge difference to the environment.

You split your players as 3*4. Nothing much wrong with that but would
2*6 be a good alternative? I was running a Shadowfist event on the
same day. This was double-elim and it worked out that we had 6
winners going into the final stage. I offered them the choice of a
6-player game or 2*3 followed by a duel. The voting was evenly split
so I used my casting vote to make it a 6-player (I like big games).
This was risky as it might have gone on forever but, as it happened,
the play was aggressive and it finished in just over an hour.

I've run Doomtown with up to 11 players in one game and think
something like this is a great format for VTES. LMK if you ever set
one up.

Andrew

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
Newsgroups snipped.

In message <9F5D0B40FB5B3015.2CC12597...@lp.airnew
s.net>, Andrew S. Davidson <a...@csi.com> writes

>I've run Doomtown with up to 11 players in one game and think
>something like this is a great format for VTES.

It's an absolutely terrible format for V:TES. Being able to keep track
of what's on the table becomes nigh on impossible, even for rules
purposes rather than strategic (e.g. are you contesting something?)

Vote decks become seriously destabilised as a strategic force, because
of the fact that it becomes extremely difficult to gain anything even
remotely resembling vote-lock, even with table talk.

Combat decks end up being seriously screwed card-wise. It's not
impossible, even with 5 players, for a serious combat deck to end up
running out of cards.

Maintaining a sensible state of play is difficult, because it can take
an extremely long time for your turn to come round again. This doubles
up with added difficulties of what happens if someone ends up screwed
early on (which is more than possible) and gets ousted early by a fast
deck. They end up sitting round for *hours*, or having wasted their
time travelling etc. completely if you cut down the number of rounds to,
say, 1.

The game can take a *huge* amount of time to play. Something similar
was attempted at a European GenCon (back when it was EuroGenCon, rather
than GenConUK, IIRC) ending up taking 7 or 8 hours. Matt Green can
probably provide more details. '96, I believe.
